title: What If a Man Released Starlings in Central Park? 200 Million

scenes.text: What if a few dozen birds released in one park ended up on an entire continent?
In 1890, Eugene Schieffelin set European starlings free in New York's Central Park.
The story goes that he wanted every bird from Shakespeare's plays in America.
The starlings survived their first winters, then multiplied. Within fifty years they had spread across the continent.
Within a century there were an estimated 200 million, taking over nest cavities from native birds.
Today they cause about 800 million dollars in farm damage a year. All from one park.
